name: Labor Vector meta-aggregator: worked questions
note: Each question is paired with the kind of evidence that can answer it and the census records that hold that evidence, by each record's own answers and does_not_answer fields. The gap is the part of the question no record in the census settles. The roles and gaps are readings.

questions.question: Where are actual negotiated protections against automated monitoring and discipline?
questions.why: A protection is evidence when it is written into an agreement or a rule. Contract text and policy instruments hold it; estimates and testimony do not.

resources.role: U.S. union contract provisions on notice, information, monitoring, data rights and job security, each linked to its agreement
laws, policies and EU platform-work collective agreements, including rules on algorithmic management
organizing toolkits and examples of pro-worker contract language on automation and AI

questions.gap: None of the three records whether a provision is enforced or what it changes at work.

questions.question: Which sources observe employment change, and which estimate exposure?
questions.why: An exposure estimate scores what AI could do to a task; an observed outcome counts what happened to jobs. They answer different questions and are often cited as if they answered the same one.

resources.role: observed: employment by age and AI exposure in ADP payroll records, monthly
observed: occupational churn and unemployment by exposure, from the CPS
estimated: the technical feasibility of GenAI automation, task by task, for occupations worldwide
estimated from use: an applicability score built from Bing Copilot conversations
observed use on one provider's product: the share of O*NET tasks performed with Claude

questions.gap: No record establishes that exposure causes the employment change; the two observed trackers reach different readings of the same period.

questions.question: Who does the data work that trains AI, and on what terms?
questions.why: The labor inside training and evaluation is recorded by the workers themselves, by ratings against labor standards, and by guidance to the companies that buy it. Each holds a different part.

resources.role: inquiries written by data workers on their own workplaces, pay and organizing
platforms rated against five fair-work principles, with a survey of 776 cloudworkers
workers' ratings of Mechanical Turk requesters on pay, fairness and communication
guidance to AI practitioners on paying and sourcing data enrichment workers

questions.gap: None gives wages or conditions at the scale of the industry, or how much of a given system's training data any reported work produced.

questions.question: What does automated management of workers look like, and can a worker see the data it uses?
questions.why: The products, the rules that govern them and the data a worker can recover are three different records of the same direction of labor.

resources.role: an inventory of workplace technology products, 2020 to 2021, with their stated terms on consent and worker access to data
data obtained for gig workers from platforms, on how work was allocated, paid and assessed
the rules that address algorithmic management on platforms

questions.gap: The product inventory is a 2021 snapshot, and no record measures how often or with what effect a product is used at a workplace.

questions.question: How do people use AI systems in their own work, and how is that use recorded?
questions.why: A provider's record of its own users, a classification of one assistant's conversations, and a benchmark of constructed tasks each describe labor performed with AI from a different position.

resources.role: Claude conversations mapped to tasks and collaboration modes, with task success as Claude assesses it: one provider's own product
Bing Copilot conversations, 2024, classified as user goals and AI actions
frontier models' deliverables on tasks built from professionals' work, graded against experts'

questions.gap: None records, from the commissioning side, whether the system's labor advanced the task the user set, or who receives the time it saves. That is the question DSL measures.

questions.question: Who receives the gains of labor performed with or for AI, and who bears the costs?
questions.why: The census's organizing question in its sharpest form. Its records hold costs more often than gains.

resources.role: costs as observed: employment of young workers in exposed occupations against its counterfactual
pay and conditions on the platforms rated, against minimum standards
estimated time savings by task, without who captures them
no clear labor-market footprint yet, at the level the CPS can see

questions.gap: No record in the census measures the distribution of productivity gains between workers, employers, platforms and model providers.
